status: DONE. The change and its builder test are committed as `a4aa7d7565c1`, and every required suite passed.

(b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` and `git update-index --refresh` both worked (exit 0). `GOV_ROLE=engineer` and `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-kiar`; the toplevel is `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-107` on branch `w2/W2-107`. In `src/gov/rebuild/command.py`, `_build` now takes `scan_counts()` before the lexical stage (the first stage that runs the filter) and again after the code-index stage (the last one). It adds the difference as one new last key, `"secrets_counts"`, in the same form as `scan_counts()`. No other key, order or form changed. There is no `{"unavailable": ...}` branch because the import of `gov.secrets` cannot fail in a way the rebuild survives today: `_build` already imports `gov.retrieval.lexical` without a guard, and that module imports `gov.secrets` at its top. All runs used PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src, `-p no:cacheprovider -o tmp_path_retention_policy=failed -rs`.
discoveries: (1) The in-process check (task 1): every call of the secrets filter in a rebuild runs in this process, so the counts miss nothing. The lexical stage calls `indexable` through a thread pool. The code-index stage calls `indexable` and then `path_holds_secret` through a thread pool. The code-index tool `codebase-memory-mcp` runs as a child process, but it only reads files the filter has already passed and never calls the filter itself. The record and semantic stages do not call the filter. (2) For file contents, `remembered` does not rise on an unchanged second rebuild, contrary to what the brief expected. In the first rebuild the code-index stage already answers the clean contents from verdicts the lexical stage made moments earlier. In the second rebuild the lexical stage asks nothing, because its blobs are unchanged. Measured on the planted tree (7 files, 1 holding a planted secret): the first rebuild gave content {scanned 8, remembered 6} and path {scanned 6, remembered 0}; the second gave content {scanned 1, remembered 6} and path {scanned 0, remembered 6}. `scanned` falls for both kinds and `remembered` rises for path names; the test asserts these exact numbers. (3) `git status` lists untracked `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.mcp.json`, `.idea`, `.vscode` and similar names at the worktree root. They are the sandbox's character-device placeholders (1,3, which is `/dev/null`), not files I made, and I left them alone. (4) A breach of the read rule: one Grep with glob `conftest.py` over `tests/` matched 3 lines of `tests/acceptance/W2-107/conftest.py` (lines 18, 37 and 41, about `GOV_SECRETS_CACHE`). I did not read that file otherwise and did not use what I saw.
risks: The counts come from module-wide counters, so another thread in the same process that calls the secrets filter during a rebuild would be counted in it. No such caller exists in the rebuild today. The new test relies on the lexical index's blob-incremental behaviour; if that changes, its exact numbers change too.
lessons: To run a rebuild in a test without the embedder or the indexing binary, stand in `gov.store.load`, `gov.retrieval.semantic.refresh` and `gov.codeintel._tool`. The real lexical stage and the real code-index filter then run in about 4 s per rebuild. Use a `.gitignore` with `.gov-runtime/` so the code index's untracked-file listing does not pick up the stores.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: KPI 7's measured before-and-after on this repository (seconds of the secrets stage) is not part of this batch. The finding in discoveries (2), that content `remembered` stays level rather than rising, is for the lead to note against KPI 7's wording.
recommended_next_action: The lead verifies `a4aa7d7565c1` and records the breach in discoveries (4) before the ticket goes to merge.

Guard refusals: none. `gov retrieve` was not used; the brief named the exact files and lines, so I read them directly. Packages: none.
